message.content:
This is a CBP ruling on Nero Mist, which the laboratory found to be an "other igneous stone" (not granite). Slabs of that size and thickness, surface-worked, would be classified in heading 6802, "Monumental or building stone, worked... other than slate."

Subheading 6802.99 covers other worked stone. Within heading 6802, 6802.10 covers tiles, cubes and similar articles with a largest surface area under 7 cm square. 6802.21 to 6802.29 cover other stone of calcareous type, such as marble, travertine and alabaster. 6802.91 covers other marble, travertine and alabaster. 6802.93 covers granite, and 6802.99 covers other stone.

Since this is not granite, it falls under 6802.99. The statistical suffixes are 6802.99.0040 for other stone, and 6802.99.0020 for slate, which is not relevant here. I recall 6802.99.00 having 10-digit breakouts: 6802.99.0010 for "Other: Of a thickness not exceeding 2.5 cm", or something like that. I am not certain of this, so I am going with the general "other" number.

Because I cannot confirm the breakouts, I choose 6802.99.0090, the residual "Other" line.

{"hts_code": "6802.99.0090", "reason": "Surface-worked slabs of other igneous stone (not granite) for countertops are worked monumental or building stone of heading 6802, falling under the other worked stone subheading 6802.99; I am not certain of the 10-digit statistical suffix."}
